entry_conditions: Supported on the same fixed-base Panda/controller with both object poses, corresponding goals, qpos/qvel and two causal TCP/object states. Positions and goals are world metres, orientations wxyz; qpos 7:9 are individual finger positions. Initial demonstrated entry has fingers 0.04 m each, TCP world z about 0.442 m and stationary source cubes at z 0.020 m. The second expanded entry is incoming red over red_goal in xy, held with fingers about 0.0183 m each and descending at red center world z 0.084-0.169 m while blue remains at its source. Internal supported entries include red already released and retreating, traversal to blue, and approach/closure/lift of the selected block. Both pose histories, gripper width and qvel help distinguish these cases. At the API level the intended next object must agree with demonstrated red-first then blue scene context. Unlike the source hypothesis, this executable forward has no intended-object token: it learns latent role attention from state and goals and cannot independently accept a conflicting request or an unseen free-space reinitialization.
exit_conditions: Useful late acquisition exit is the selected cube elevated and co-moving with the near-downward TCP, closed fingers around 0.0183 m each (total width about 0.0365 m), and beginning goalward translation with the demonstrated command -1. Measured expanded endpoints have red center world z about 0.280-0.283 m or blue 0.287-0.293 m, nonzero arm qvel, and TCP wxyz near [0,1,0,0]. These are observed support, not enforced tolerances or requirements for zero speed. Observed TCP world x is approximately 0.008-0.010 m behind the object; do not demand exact centering. Closure without subsequent object elevation is not enough. Earlier transfer during aligned approach/close/lift is possible because deliver_block shares those phases; preserve the same payload identity and do not introduce an opening at transfer.
overlap_role: This model is trained on all 24 expanded slices without filtering transitions. In the 149-154-action incoming-placement overlaps it learns red lowering while closed, opening/releasing near the tray goal, vertical retreat and traversal toward blue. In the 106-122-action acquisition overlaps it learns selected-block final approach, closure, lift and initial goalward translation. Demo10300 has overlaps [75,182), [265,415) and [445,562). Shared pose-and-goal encoders expose both TCP-relative and world geometry; continuous scene-conditioned role attention can retain incoming red and prospective blue together rather than hard-switching a reference at a world pose. This represents training coverage and model structure, not verified closed-loop success or a programmed phase schedule.
successor_readiness: Deliver_block should receive the SAME intended payload identity at the API level, its matching goal, both object poses, full qpos/qvel and uninterrupted causal TCP history. For a late handoff, object/TCP displacement should remain approximately constant as the object rises or moves goalward; retain closed grip rather than opening due to policy change. For an early handoff, the successor must be willing to continue descent, close and lift, not assume that a closed-finger or geometric alignment cue already proves a stable grasp. If the next requested object is blue but incoming red is still descending, red goal alignment is not readiness to carry blue: either continue this acquisition model through release/retreat or transfer only to a policy supporting that exact incoming phase. This package has no externally settable role token, so the successor and selector must keep identity consistent through their own interface rather than assuming an extra channel exists here.
failure_signatures: Intended object conflicts with the scene/order supported by training; attention/action behavior addresses an already settled cube instead of the source; TCP-to-source xy error increases during descent; fingers close but the object stays at table height; object-to-TCP displacement grows during lift; incoming red is moved laterally before release; or red is disturbed while acquiring blue. Pose co-motion and finger opening are observable cues, not proof of contact or force closure. Inspected offsets are millimetre-scale; larger grasp errors and recovery maneuvers are unsupported, not prevented by coded constraints.
continuation_guidance: Replan from the most recent two causal states; the fixed executor runs eight actions per sampled 16-action chunk. Continue through supported lowering/opening/retreat when red is over its goal and blue is next, using red z motion, finger widening and TCP retreat relative to stationary red as distinguishing information. Once approaching the intended source, continue while aligned descent, closure and elevation are progressing. Prefer a delivery transfer when elevation plus co-motion and incipient goalward movement indicate the observed useful exit; transfer earlier only if the successor supports approach/close/lift. Do not stop solely because TCP xy is aligned, fingers have closed, or incoming red meets its geometric goal. The model has no runtime termination gate, elapsed-time phase schedule or hard numerical entry/exit thresholds. The selector chooses continuation versus transfer from observation evidence. Task success remains the supplied red_at_goal AND blue_at_goal contract; it imposes no extra release, clearance, speed or sustained-hold condition.
limitations: Observed demonstrations establish transition support only. No closed-loop performance has been measured in this design session. The executable model uses two states rather than the heuristic's four, eight executed actions rather than two, and implicit learned role queries rather than an unavailable explicit next-object token. Arbitrary color requests, order reversal, large source shifts, unseen yaw, dropped-block recovery and novel robot configurations are not supported claims. The shared representation is symmetric to jointly relabeling pose/goal slots, but absolute world/base information is retained and physical translation/rotation equivariance is not claimed. Grasp/contact is inferred from elevation and co-motion, not sensed. There are no hard IK, collision, joint-limit or stability constraints, and the shared full-demonstration normalizer is never refitted on the skill slice.
